title: Weighted and rank-two extensions of Patel's proof: Hemmer–Straub–Westrem's Ev character-average conjecture

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: Extending Patel's pointwise proof (2026, Solution 1), we give an alternative coefficient proof of Conjecture 17, equation (6.1), page 15, of Hemmer, Straub and Westrem's New identities in the character table of symmetric groups involving Riordan numbers (2026), recovering the two-binary-quadratic Hilbert series of Benanti et al. (2012, Example 3.3, p.160). Both weighted character sums vanish in odd degree and equal binomial(n/2+2,2) in even degree. Patel's three-variable Schur specialization first identifies the sums for each partition, retaining all multiplicities in Ev. The cycle-index generating function then reduces their weighted average to a constant term equal to (1-t^2)^(-3). We give explicit arbitrary-weight and common-divisor consequences, including the N=1 case of Amdeberhan's q-series conjecture, and rederive the Riordan tableau formula already implicit in Meilhan–Suzuki (2015). A companion adjoint-representation argument proves the N=2 instances of the source's two character identities and its q-series conjecture.
summary: An alternative coefficient proof and explicit Ev-character application of the invariant Hilbert series evaluated by Benanti et al. (2012), extending Patel’s full pointwise solution (2026). The written consequences include Riordan and equal-part formulas with prior attribution, mixed common divisors, first-row vanishing, arbitrary multiplicative weights and the N=1 q-series. The full Motzkin-level path question is answered by Amaral–Gil–Weiner (2026). The rank-two companion proves both character identities and the q-series conjecture for N=2, using the exceptional symplectic/orthogonal adjoint identification.

coverage.scope: No all-N theorem or new character-degree refinement is asserted.

verification.formal_statements: The result declarations in the linked Lean files prove the weighted and pointwise identities in the Frobenius-coefficient model. The ordinary-character interpretation uses the classical Frobenius formula; an internal Specht-module construction is separate.
verification.written_proofs: The all-degree Schur detector, including odd-degree same-parity triples; pointwise identity; weighted generating function; Riordan and equal-part formulas; common-divisor count; first-row vanishing; arbitrary-weight and N=1 q-series consequences. The N=2 pointwise identity via the adjoint representations of SO(5) and Sp(4), with its weighted and q-series consequences.
verification.finite_checks: Exact Murnaghan–Nakayama character sums for all 67 partitions with 0<=n<=8; cycle-index Laurent coefficients through degree 60; q-series through degree 10; all 274 monomial-symmetric basis elements through degree 18; Riordan/tableau degrees through 30; equal parts with 1<=r<=15 and 1<=k<=5; common-divisor cases through size 12; first-row vanishing through n=5; a signed multiplicative-weight specialization through degree 10; the Appendix A counterexample at lambda=(5,2,1),N=3. Detailed counts are in verification.txt. The N=2 pointwise identity is checked by Murnaghan–Nakayama on all 30 partitions with 0<=n<=6.
